| Deck size | 60 (36 spells, 24 lands) |
| Average mana value | 3.44 |
| Primary win | Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Weftstalker Ardent turn each entering creature into damage to each opponent; warp casts and token makers multiply the number of entries per turn |
| Secondary win | Combat with warped fliers (Nova Hellkite, Exalted Sunborn) behind a pumped token board, with Rogue's Passage clearing the last blocker |

## Overview

Warp lets you cast a card for its warp cost instead of its mana cost, exiles it at the beginning
of the next end step, and then lets you cast it from exile on a later turn. That single line gives
the deck two things at once: a permanent that enters the battlefield for far less than its printed
price, and a card that is not spent when it leaves — it comes back as a real card in exile, ready
to be cast again when the mana is there.

The deck converts those entries into damage. Three cards are paid for the same resource: Impact
Tremors, Warleader's Call and Weftstalker Ardent each deal 1 damage to every opponent when a
creature you control enters. With all three on the battlefield a single creature entering is 3
damage; with Delney, Streetwise Lookout doubling Weftstalker Ardent's trigger it is 4. Warp keeps
supplying entries for two mana, and the token makers — Knight Luminary, Rayblade Trooper, Exalted
Sunborn, Fountainport — turn one entry into three.

| Engine piece | Copies | What it does |
|--------------|--------|--------------|
| Weftstalker Ardent | 4 | Warp {R}. A 2/3 that pings each opponent whenever another creature or artifact you control enters, and one of the cheapest re-entries in the deck |
| Impact Tremors | 4 | Two mana, one damage to each opponent per creature entering. The deck's cheapest payoff and the reason a two-mana warp is a real clock |
| Warleader's Call | 3 | Damage on entry plus +1/+1 to the whole team, so the same tokens that ping also win combat |
| Tannuk, Steadfast Second | 3 | Other creatures you control have haste, so warped bodies attack the turn they land; also the Kavu that makes Possibility Technician's exiled cards castable |
| Delney, Streetwise Lookout | 2 | Doubles the triggered abilities of creatures with power 2 or less — Weftstalker Ardent, Rayblade Trooper and All-Fates Stalker all qualify |
| Knight Luminary | 3 | Warp {1}{W} for a 3/2 that brings a 1/1 Soldier with it. One warped entry becomes two drain triggers, four with Exalted Sunborn |
| Possibility Technician | 2 | Warp {1}{R}. Every Kavu entry exiles the top card of your library and lets you play it while you control a Kavu, so the warp loop also draws |
| Haliya, Guided by Light | 2 | Warp {W}. One life per entry, and a card at end of turn once you have gained three |

## Approach

### Game plan by phase

1. Turns one and two: Impact Tremors is the best opening in the deck, and Lightning Helix is the
   interaction that keeps you alive while the enchantments come down. A warped Knight Luminary or
   Weftstalker Ardent on turn two is already two damage per opponent before any attack.
2. Turns three and four: add the second and third payoff. Warleader's Call pumps the board,
   Weftstalker Ardent stacks another point per entry, and Delney doubles it. Tannuk, Steadfast
   Second gives the team haste, which matters because most of the bodies only live for one turn.
3. Turns five and up: token doubling and reach. Exalted Sunborn makes every Soldier and every
   Rayblade Trooper death token into two, Fountainport adds a Fish every turn, and Rogue's Passage
   pushes a 4/5 flier or a pumped token through for the last points.

### Card roles

| Role | Cards | Copies | Function |
|------|-------|--------|----------|
| Drain payoffs | Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Weftstalker Ardent | 4, 3, 4 | Convert creature entries into damage to each opponent; they are the deck's clock |
| Trigger doubler | Delney, Streetwise Lookout | 2 | Doubles the ping from Weftstalker Ardent and the counter trigger from Rayblade Trooper |
| Warp bodies | Weftstalker Ardent, Knight Luminary, Haliya, Rayblade Trooper, Exalted Sunborn, Nova Hellkite, Weftblade Enhancer, Possibility Technician, All-Fates Stalker | 4, 3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1 | Every one of them is a cheap entry now and a castable card later |
| Enablers | Tannuk, Steadfast Second, Memorial Team Leader | 3, 1 | Haste for one-turn bodies, the Kavu body that turns on Possibility Technician, and a team pump during your turn |
| Token makers | Knight Luminary, Rayblade Trooper, Exalted Sunborn, Fountainport | 3, 3, 2, 2 | Multiply entries per spell; Exalted Sunborn doubles every token made |
| Card advantage | Possibility Technician, Haliya, Guided by Light | 2, 2 | Exile-and-play off Kavu entries, and a draw at end of turn off three points of lifegain |
| Interaction | Lightning Helix, All-Fates Stalker, Nova Hellkite | 2, 1, 2 | Three damage plus three life, a temporary exile on a creature, and a ping on entry |

### Lands as engines

| Land | Copies | What it does for the deck |
|------|--------|---------------------------|
| Fountainport | 2 | Three mana and a tap makes a 1/1 blue Fish, which is another drain trigger on every payoff; spare tokens can be sacrificed for a card instead |
| Rogue's Passage | 2 | Four mana and a tap makes a creature unblockable, which is how a warped Nova Hellkite or a pumped Soldier finishes a game through a stalled board |
| Evolving Wilds | 2 | Finds whichever basic the hand is missing, and the land entering is not a trigger this deck cares about, so the tapped entry costs little |
| Plains | 10 | The heavier colour: Exalted Sunborn wants two white, and Knight Luminary, Rayblade Trooper, Haliya and Weftblade Enhancer all want white |
| Mountain | 8 | Red for Weftstalker Ardent, Tannuk, Steadfast Second, Possibility Technician and Nova Hellkite, with two Mountains needed for the double red cards |

| Cost | Count | Cards |

| Two | 6 | Impact Tremors, Lightning Helix |

Twenty-four lands, twenty white sources and nineteen red ones once Evolving Wilds is counted for
either. The printed curve is deliberately top-heavy: the four, five and six mana cards are all
warp cards, so their real cost on the turn that matters is two or three mana, and only the cards
you draw late are paid for in full.

## Gameplay strategy

### Early game

Lead with Impact Tremors whenever it is in the opening hand; it turns every later warp into
damage and costs only two mana. On turn two the correct play is usually a warped one: Knight
Luminary for two mana brings a Soldier, Weftstalker Ardent for one red mana is the cheapest ping
in the deck, and Haliya for one white mana starts the lifegain count that draws cards later.
Lightning Helix is for the creature that would otherwise eat your enchantments, not for the face.
The warped permanent leaving at end of turn is not a loss: it goes to exile and stays castable.

### Mid game

Turns three to five are about stacking payoffs. Warleader's Call is the single most important
card in the mid game because it both pings and pumps, which is what lets a board of 1/1 Soldiers
actually attack. Tannuk, Steadfast Second is what makes the plan work on the turn it is played:
the whole team has haste, so a warped Nova Hellkite or a Knight Luminary can attack immediately
and then leave at end of turn with its damage already dealt. Delney is the other key piece, since
doubling Weftstalker Ardent doubles the deck's main clock.

### The combo turn

The deck's best turn is a two-mana warp that becomes four entries. With Impact Tremors,
Warleader's Call and Weftstalker Ardent on the battlefield, and Delney out, every creature that
enters deals 4 damage to each opponent. Warp Knight Luminary for two mana: the Knight is one
entry, and with Exalted Sunborn on the battlefield its Soldier is doubled into two more. Three
entries is 12 damage to each opponent for two mana, and the same turn the Soldiers are 1/1s with
Warleader's Call's +1/+1 on them. Recast the same Knight from exile later in the game for four
mana and do it again; Possibility Technician turns each Kavu entry into an extra card off the top,
so the loop refuels itself.

### Win condition two

When the drain is not enough, the deck attacks. Nova Hellkite is a 4/5 flier with haste that also
pings a creature on entry, Exalted Sunborn is a 4/5 flier with lifelink that doubles every token
you make, and Warleader's Call plus Memorial Team Leader make even the Soldier tokens into a real
board. Rogue's Passage is the finisher: four mana makes the largest body unblockable, which is
usually the difference between a stalled board and lethal. Fountainport belongs to this plan too,
since a free 1/1 each turn both adds to the attack and triggers all three drain payoffs.

### Mulligan guide

Keep two or three lands with at least one Impact Tremors or Weftstalker Ardent, plus a cheap warp
card to cast. Hands with two payoffs and no action are worse than they look, because the payoffs
do nothing alone. Ship hands that need double white or double red on turn three without the
matching basics, and ship hands whose only plays cost four or more unless Tannuk is among them,
since Tannuk is what makes those cards castable early.

### Key interactions and edge cases

- Warp exiles the permanent at the beginning of the next end step, so a warped creature gets
  exactly one combat step and then leaves. Attack first, then let it go.
- An exiled warped card can be cast again on a later turn, but that cast pays the printed cost,
  not the warp cost. Warp is a discount once per copy, not a permanent discount.
- All-Fates Stalker exiles a creature until it leaves the battlefield, so warping it out returns
  the creature you removed. Cast it for four mana when you want the exile to stick.
- Delney only doubles creatures with power 2 or less: Weftstalker Ardent, Rayblade Trooper and
  All-Fates Stalker qualify, while Haliya, Knight Luminary, Tannuk and Possibility Technician do
  not.
- Haliya's draw needs three or more life gained in the same turn. Three entries does it, and so
  does any entry plus Lightning Helix.
- Rayblade Trooper only makes its Soldier when a nontoken creature with a +1/+1 counter dies.
  Warped creatures are exiled, not destroyed, so the trigger usually comes from a counter placed
  by Rayblade Trooper itself or by Weftblade Enhancer.
- Tannuk, Steadfast Second is legendary. Warping a second copy while one is on the battlefield
  means one of them dies to the legend rule, so hold the second copy until the first is gone.
- Possibility Technician needs a Kavu on the battlefield to cast the card it exiles. It is a Kavu
  itself, so it works alone, but if it is removed the exiled card is stranded until Tannuk or
  Memorial Team Leader arrives.
- Exalted Sunborn doubles tokens, not entries: the two Soldiers it creates are two separate
  drain triggers, which is exactly why it is in the deck.

### Matchups

Against aggro the deck is a favourite after sideboarding in spirit rather than in cards: Lightning
Helix and All-Fates Stalker buy the turns, and Weftstalker Ardent plus Impact Tremors race small
creature decks well because the damage does not require attacking. Against midrange the plan is to
grind: every warped card is a second card later, and the drain payoffs do not care about blockers.
Against control the deck wants Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call down before the sweeper, since
enchantments survive creature removal, and Delney makes the Soldier tokens unblockable against
large blockers. Against combo there is no counterspell in the list, so the deck has to race with
the drain plan and use Rogue's Passage for the last points.

## Iterations

| Round | Change | Metrics |
|-------|--------|---------|
| v1 | First build: added Roaming Throne, two Bygone Colossus, two Windcrag Siege, three Delney and two Lightning Helix | synergy 69.6 (below the 70 gate), sim 53.7 percent, T4 0.640, P(4 lands by turn 4) 0.644 |
| v1 to v2 | minus 1 Roaming Throne, minus 2 Bygone Colossus, minus 1 Windcrag Siege, minus 1 Lightning Helix, minus 1 Delney, plus 2 Weftblade Enhancer, plus 2 Possibility Technician, plus 1 All-Fates Stalker (trade the expensive colorless top end for cards that share the Drix and Kavu text and actually enter the battlefield) | synergy 69.6 to 71.3, sim 53.7 to 60.3 percent, T4 0.640 to 0.619, P(4 lands) 0.644 to 0.616 |
| v2 to v3 | minus 1 Windcrag Siege, plus 1 Memorial Team Leader (the third Kavu turns on Possibility Technician and its pump is what makes the Soldier tokens attack) | synergy 71.3 to 71.1, sim 60.3 to 66.0 percent, T4 0.619 to 0.637, P(4 lands) 0.616 to 0.640 |

A third variant, swapping All-Fates Stalker for Stone-Giant of High Pass, passed every gate but
simulated at 58.0 percent against 66.0 percent for this list, so the current build was kept.

Battery gates for the final list: 60 cards, no missing cards, Standard legal, zero rotating
cards, simulated win rate 66.0 percent over three 500-game runs, synergy 71.1, goldfish turn-four
consistency 0.637, probability of four lands by turn four 0.640.
